record.context_brief: Ill-posedness degree of the composite Hausdorff moment operator
record.original_question: Let J: L2(0,1) -> L2(0,1) be the integration operator [Jx](s) = integral_0^s x(t) dt for 0 <= s <= 1, and let A := B^(H) o J: L2(0,1) -> l2. Is the inverse problem Ax = y moderately ill-posed, in the sense that there exist constants C > 0 and kappa > 0 such that C i^(-kappa) <= sigma_i(A) for all i in N, or is it instead exponentially ill-posed?

evidence.quote: we combine the compact integration operator J : L2 (0, 1) -> L2 (0, 1) defined as [Jx](s) := integral_0^s x(t)dt (0 <= s <= 1) with B (H) from (1) in the operator equation Ax = y, where the forward operator is here the composition A := B (H) o J : L2 (0, 1) -> l2 .

Definition 1. Let A be a compact operator mapping between Hilbert spaces with non-closed range. If there exists a constant C > 0 and an exponent 0 < kappa < infinity such that C i^(-kappa) <= sigma_i (A) for all i in N, we call the operator equation (4) moderately ill-posed of degree at most kappa. If (6) does not hold for arbitrarily large kappa, we call (4) severely ill-posed. Typical behaviour of severely ill-posed equations is exponential ill-posedness.
Open Question 2: Is the operator equation (4) with the composite operator A from (5) moderately ill-posed or, in contrast, even exponentially ill-posed?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $L^2(0,1)$ denote the Hilbert space of (equivalence classes of) square-integrable real-valued functions on $(0,1)$ with its standard inner product, and let $\ell^2$ denote the Hilbert space of square-summable real sequences indexed by $\mathbb{N}=\{1,2,3,\dots\}$.

Define the integration operator
$$J:L^2(0,1)\to L^2(0,1),\qquad [Jx](s)=\int_0^s x(t)\,dt,\quad 0\le s\le 1,$$
and the Hausdorff moment operator
$$B^{(H)}:L^2(0,1)\to\ell^2,\qquad B^{(H)}x=\Bigl(\int_0^1 t^{i-1}\,x(t)\,dt\Bigr)_{i\in\mathbb{N}}.$$
Both operators are bounded and linear; $J$ is compact, while $B^{(H)}$ is bounded but non-compact. Consider their composition
$$A:=B^{(H)}\circ J:L^2(0,1)\to\ell^2,$$
which is a compact linear operator with non-closed range. Let $\sigma_1(A)\ge\sigma_2(A)\ge\cdots>0$ denote the singular values of $A$ arranged in non-increasing order.

Call the equation $Ax=y$ moderately ill-posed of degree at most $\kappa$ if there exist constants $C>0$ and $0<\kappa<\infty$ such that
$$C\,i^{-\kappa}\;\le\;\sigma_i(A)\qquad\text{for all }i\in\mathbb{N},$$
and severely ill-posed otherwise; the typical behaviour in the severely ill-posed case being exponential decay $\sigma_i(A)\lesssim e^{-ci}$ for some $c>0$.

Question: Is the equation $Ax=y$ moderately ill-posed (i.e. is there a polynomial lower bound $C\,i^{-\kappa}\le\sigma_i(A)$ for some finite $\kappa$), or is it exponentially (severely) ill-posed?
artifact.category_tag: Ill-posed inverse problems and singular value decay
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent work studying compositions of the Hausdorff moment operator with the integration operator established two-sided bounds $e^{-\bar c\, i}\le\sigma_i(A)\le \bar c\, i^{-3/2}$ for large $i$, but explicitly states that it remains unresolved whether the composition is moderately ill-posed or exponentially ill-posed. No publication appears to definitively settle the dichotomy.

status_evidence.title: Curious ill-posedness phenomena in the composition of non-compact linear operators in Hilbert spaces (arXiv:2401.14701)
status_evidence.snippet: exp(−c̄·i) ≤ σ_i(T) ≤ c̄/i^(3/2) ... it could not be cleared if T = H·J really leads to an exponentially (severely) ill-posed problem or whether it leads to a moderate ill-posed problem.
status_evidence.claim: Best known bounds leave the moderate-vs-exponential dichotomy unresolved.

status_evidence.title: The degree of ill-posedness of composite linear ill-posed problems (arXiv:2111.01036)
status_evidence.snippet: Singular values of the composition decay faster than those of the integration operator; gap between available lower bounds and the obtained upper bound.
status_evidence.claim: There is a gap between the known lower and upper bounds for σ_i of the composition.
